title: eryngium tricuspidatum subsp. bocconei
intro: Eryngium tricuspidatum subsp. bocconei, commonly known as Boccone's eryngo, is a plant species in the carrot family that is native to the Mediterranean region. The plant has been traditionally used in folk medicine for its potential health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties that may aid in wound healing and the treatment of respiratory issues such as bronchitis and asthma. The therapeutic actions of Boccone's eryngo include its ability to stimulate digestion and relieve flatulence, as well as its anti-spasmodic and anti-emetic effects. The bioactive constituents of Eryngium tricuspidatum subsp. bocconei include flavonoids, terpenoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal properties and potential health benefits.
